title: Beyond Your Five Senses
summary: Steve Lee, Bill Poon and Valentin host in the studio while David Choe participates only through an early speakerphone call. That call immediately supplies the episode's strongest privacy lesson: David objects when a private will-related conversation is exposed without warning, then endorses the cast continuing the show without him. He describes intensive therapy, attention practice, food experiments and Steve's prospective rap album before leaving the call. The studio then moves from friendship anxiety into Peggy Kane, electronic voice phenomena, reverse speech, reptilians, lower astral planes, dream portals and alleged suppressed human abilities. Steve and Valentin add haunting stories, including experiences involving hallucinogens and a young sibling. The record preserves all of these claims as beliefs or reported perceptions while refusing to present them as verified supernatural or medical facts. A discussion of schizophrenia is especially important: the speakers wonder whether voices could be paranormal, but this is medically unsupported and can stigmatize people with psychosis. The title phrase emerges directly from that debate. The Sewol ferry disaster shifts the conversation toward obedience, Korean parenting, drowning and other distressing deaths. Alex then explains the show's labor transition, why commitment mattered more than preexisting technical skill, and how DVDASA began. The final half mixes Critter and David origin stories, creative-work philosophy, household nicknames, exercise, reproductive and racialized jokes, conflicting cast-origin memories, a secret studio redesign, Bigfoot, sexualized show-format ideas, camping, Steve's album, nail art and trivia. Every idea is retained. The transcript keeps literal speech separate from annotations: it does not replace 'health podcast' or 'Grammy Boys,' append a legal name to Dan the Automator, or insert a Reddit explanation into a spoken date. Two empty zero-duration records are the only valid cleaner drops. David's phone presence ends around 16 minutes; with zero diarized turns and zero identity windows, no line receives a published speaker name.
source_notes: Both cleaner removals are empty zero-duration records at 1088.40 and 5721.38 seconds; raw and clean word counts are identical.

The automated review queue is empty, but four vocabulary proposals are editorial rewrites rather than transcript repairs: health podcast, Dan the Automator, Grammy Boys, and November 2nd, 2012 remain literal.
The opening names Steve Lee, Bill Poon and Valentin as hosts. David Choe is absent from the studio but audibly joins by phone until roughly 960 seconds; Asa Akira is absent.
The proper open-set target is therefore DAVID_CHOE_REMOTE_PHONE during the bounded call and abstention afterward—not episode-wide presence or absence.
Peggy Kane, EVP, reverse speech, reptilians, lower astral planes, dream portals, hauntings and Bigfoot are speaker claims or experiences, not independently established facts.
Hallucinogen context stays attached to two apparition accounts. The transcript does not diagnose the speakers or use the stories as proof of a supernatural cause.
The discussion that treats schizophrenia or hearing voices as possible paranormal ability is preserved as an idea but marked medically unsupported and potentially stigmatizing.
The Korean ferry discussion is identifiable as the Sewol disaster from context, but the cast's cultural explanation is opinion and not a verified causal account.
The guest who left after disagreeing with show rules, private partners, family members, a young sibling, locations, clients and current schedules remain outside searchable identity metadata.
Sexualized format ideas, reproductive hypotheticals, paranormal claims, racial stereotypes and gross-out material remain in the source layer; warnings do not censor them.
speaker_policy: Episode metadata may name the explicitly introduced studio hosts and record David Choe's bounded phone presence. Because diarization produced zero turns and zero identity windows, no transcript line is assigned to David, Steve Lee, Bill Poon, Valentin, Alex or anyone else. Any future identity test must evaluate telephone-channel David separately and abstain after the call.

connections.why: The episode contains a bounded remote David call followed by a long founder-absent studio section.
Being on a private call is not consent to speakerphone publication; disclosure must precede exposure.
An ironic phrase can be explained editorially without replacing what was said.
Listening to one complete work becomes a simple resistance to constant switching.
The cast explicitly says concepts become real only when participants commit.
Treatment creates hope for growth and anxiety that a friend may change.
Named producers are possibilities, not completed album credits.
The show's criticism of its own sexual fixation should be retained beside the explicit material it critiques.
Paranormal testimony remains legible without receiving factual endorsement.
Hallucinogen use is necessary context for interpreting reported perceptions.
A sensed presence and immobility are narrated as haunting, while the archive avoids diagnosing or validating the cause.
A childhood family story may be summarized without identifying the child or residence.
Romanticizing psychosis as supernatural ability can discourage evidence-based care.
The cast uses Sewol to question whose deaths receive American attention.
Alex's role change makes the infrastructure behind the spontaneous show visible.
Technical tasks can be taught more readily than sustained care and availability.
Years of self-directed practice turn recreation into paid work.
Participant memories provide useful but conflicting evidence about DVDASA's formation.
A redesigned room is imagined as changing guest capacity, performance and conversation.
Nail art becomes both personal pleasure and a test of anticipated social stigma.
